input: Get a nutrition consultation with a registered dietitian

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The specific health or nutrition goal (weight loss, managing a condition, athletic performance, general eating habits) completely changes what kind of dietitian to seek and what to prepare.
Whether this is for themselves, a child, a family member, or a couple affects who needs to be present and what information to gather beforehand.
Whether the consultation should be in-person or virtual, and in what region, determines which providers are available and accessible.
Budget and insurance coverage are major determinants — a covered in-network visit versus an out-of-pocket private practice consultation requires very different search strategies.
How urgently the user needs the appointment shapes whether to prioritize availability over specialty fit, and what the very next action should be.
Whether they prefer a dietitian with a particular approach (e.g., intuitive eating, clinical/medical, sports nutrition, culturally specific diets) narrows the search significantly.
Knowing what a successful consultation looks like — a one-time assessment, an ongoing coaching relationship, or a formal meal plan — determines what type of service to book.

gold.taskTitle: Book a Registered Dietitian Nutrition Consultation
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to schedule and attend a professional nutrition consultation with a registered dietitian.

questions.title: What specific health or nutrition goal are you addressing?
questions.description: Identify the primary reason for the consultation, such as weight management, a medical condition like diabetes, sports performance, gut health, or general healthy eating.

questions.title: Who is this consultation for?
questions.description: Clarify whether the appointment is for the user themselves, a child, a family member, or multiple people, as this affects provider selection and session structure.

questions.title: Do you prefer an in-person or virtual appointment?
questions.description: Determine the preferred format and, if in-person, the general location or city to narrow down available providers.

questions.title: Will you be using insurance or paying out of pocket?
questions.description: Establish the payment approach, as insurance coverage requires searching for in-network providers, while self-pay opens up a broader range of private practitioners.

questions.title: How soon do you need this appointment scheduled?
questions.description: Understand the urgency so the plan can prioritize speed of availability versus finding the most specialized or preferred dietitian.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred dietary philosophy or specialist focus?
questions.description: Find out if the user wants a dietitian with a specific approach, such as intuitive eating, plant-based nutrition, cultural food traditions, or a clinical/medical focus.

questions.title: Are you looking for a one-time assessment or ongoing support?
questions.description: Determine whether the goal is a single consultation for a snapshot assessment and meal plan, or a longer-term coaching and accountability relationship.
